$comment: Invariant I-B11 (see vectors/invariants/invariants.json) — not machine-checkable from a single document, since it's a process assertion over two HTTP exchanges. This fixture is the consumer-side/reverse-proxy conformance test that RC2 §22.1 names explicitly. It documents the test; it cannot itself prove any specific consumer implementation passes it.
scenario: A consumer (or a reverse proxy / HTTP middleware in front of it) sends one guest.answer request. The provider returns 503 answer_validation_failed.

error.message: Lucy could not produce a supported answer for this request.

assertion: Within the remainder of the 22-second interaction deadline, no second request is observed on the wire carrying the same Idempotency-Key (5a6a3c4e-1b2c-4d5e-89ab-1234567890ab). This must hold for the consumer's own retry logic, for any reverse proxy sitting in front of it, and for any generic HTTP client/middleware library the consumer is built on — none of which may fall back to 'retry on 5xx' default behavior for this specific code.
how_a_provider_conformance_run_uses_this: The provider side cannot observe consumer retry behavior directly. This fixture exists so a paired protocol/end-to-end test harness (outside the provider's own process) can assert it — e.g. a test double standing in for Prime that counts requests per Idempotency-Key and fails the run if it ever sees two for this specific error code.
